newsitem.title: UK: Wilhelmshaven refinery resumes at 210,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Wilhelmshaven refinery resumes at 210,000 bpd.

text.p: The Wilhelmshaven refinery in northern Germany has resumed operations after work to raise throughput by about 20 percent to 210,000 barrels per day, the plant's manager said on Monday.
The refinery began operations late last week and has successfully been brought up to the new thoughput capacity over the weekend, said managing director Hans Van Weelden.
"There was a bit more work than anticipated," he said, but noted unforeseen minor problems often occur during routine refinery maintenance work.
The refinery, bought earlier this year by the Hamburg-based part of the Louis Dreyfus group, was due to restart last week.
Van Weelden said work at the plant involved installing new heat exchangers with a larger surface area.
This had given the plant more efficient operating characteristics and helped boost throughput capacity.
Investment is expected to total $30 million. --London newsroom, +44 171 542 4984
